title: This Shark Can Live For Almost 400 Years 🦈⏳ #shorts
description:
In 2016, scientists radiocarbon-dated the eye lenses of 28 Greenland sharks. The largest, about 5 metres long, was estimated at 392 years old (with a big margin of error) – and even the low estimate of 272 years makes it the longest-living vertebrate known. These sharks grow only about 1 cm per year, cruise at roughly 1 km/h, and females may not mature until around 150 years old.

Sources: Nielsen et al., Science (2016), NOAA Ocean Service, University of Oxford, PBS NOVA, Scientific American

scenes.text: There is a shark that can live for almost four hundred years.
scenes.headline:
THIS SHARK
LIVES 400
YEARS

scenes.text: It's the Greenland shark. It lives in the icy, dark waters of the Arctic and the North Atlantic.
In twenty sixteen, scientists dated the eye lenses of twenty eight of these sharks. The biggest one, about five meters long, was estimated at three hundred ninety two years old.
scenes.label: ESTIMATED AGE

scenes.text: Even the lowest estimate was two hundred seventy two years. So this shark was born before the United States existed.
The secret? Freezing water and a super slow life. It grows only about one centimeter per year.
scenes.label: GROWTH PER YEAR

scenes.text: It usually cruises at around one kilometer per hour.
That's way slower than you walk.
And the craziest part? Females may not have babies until they are about one hundred fifty years old.
